newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile gov't to seek new agreement on tariff cuts.
newsitem.headline: Chile gov't to seek new agreement on tariff cuts.

text.p: Chile's government will hold off on sending Congress a bill to cut import duties gradually to eight percent from 11 percent in order to seek agreement with opposition parties, Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat said on Monday.
Aninat said the Concertacion ruling centre-left coalition's talks with the main right-wing party Renovacion Nacional had stalled over the weekend.
"Although we've worked very hard and the bill is ready, it's better to shepherd it through Congress with a minimum basis of consensus," he told a news conference.
While the Concertacion has a clear majority in the lower house, in the Senate it is outnumbered by rightists and supporters of the past military dictatorship.
Aninat said the government and the opposition had earlier worked out a plan to cut tariffs by two percentage points immediately and by a further percentage point in six or seven months.
They had also agreed to initially make up for the loss in revenue by raising a stamp tax and enforcing more stringent measures to collect the IVA value added tax.
Once the full three percentage points reduction is carried out, the government would also increase taxes on petrol.
The agreement was to be signed on Monday but Renovacion Nacional called for a four percentage point cut in tariffs and for lower state spending to finance the reduction.
Both the government and the opposition believe that lower import duties will put a brake on the Chilean peso's appreciation against the dollar.
